## NL9007

The message of a warning `--no-warn-performance` turns off contains:

```text
…is not proven to be in range for…
```

[`nl9007_guard_f64_mode.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl9007_guard_f64_mode.ts) (compiled with `--number-mode f64`):

```ts
// Under `--number-mode f64` a length is an `f64`, so `i < xs.length` does not
// type-check against an `i32` index: NL9007 spells the bound
// `toI32(xs.length)`, which compiles in both modes and is credited.
export const sumAt = (xs: number[], idx: i32[]): number => {
  let total = 0
  for (const i of idx) {
    total = total + xs[i]
  }
  return total
}
```

```text
`i` is not proven to be in range for `xs` here, so this access keeps its bounds check and compares against the length on every iteration: guard it with a test that reaches the access — `if (i >= 0 && i < toI32(xs.length))` proves both ends, and an unsigned index needs only the upper one
```

## NL9011

The message of a warning `--no-warn-performance` turns off contains:

```text
…leaves arena memory behind on every pass of this loop…
```

[`nl9011_arena_loop.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl9011_arena_loop.ts):

```ts
// NL9011: a loop over a call that leaves arena memory behind, where neither a
// scope around each pass nor one around the function takes it back, names
// what refused each of them.
class Log {
  last: string = "";
}

const digits = (n: i32): string => `${n}`;

export const count = (log: Log, rounds: i32): i32 => {
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < rounds; i++) {
    total += digits(i).length;
    log.last = `${i}`;
  }
  return total;
};
```

```text
`digits` leaves arena memory behind on every pass of this loop, which cannot release it after each pass because the allocation on line 14 is stored into memory, where this analysis stops following it, and neither can `count` when it returns, so all of it lives as long as the caller's memory does. Keep what a pass allocates out of locals declared outside the loop and out of memory older than the pass, or open the loop body with `using a = arena()`
```

## NL9012

The message of a warning `--no-warn-performance` turns off contains:

```text
…` but allocates on every call, so each thread marks and releases its arena around every element. Compute the answer without building a string, an array or an object to save both
```

[`nl9012_par_alloc.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl9012_par_alloc.ts):

```ts
// NL9012: a parallel body that allocates compiles, recycled per element, and
// the call says what every element pays for it.
import { parallelReduce } from "nish/threads";

const widest = (a: i32, b: i32): i32 => (`${a}`.length > `${b}`.length ? a : b);

export const main = (): i32 => parallelReduce([7, 42, 1000], widest, 0);
```

```text
the body of this `parallelReduce` allocates per element: `widest` answers `i32` but allocates on every call, so each thread marks and releases its arena around every element. Compute the answer without building a string, an array or an object to save both
```

## NL9013

The message of a warning `--no-warn-performance` turns off contains:

```text
…so entering the range keeps its check on every iteration of this loop…
```

[`nl9013_range_entry_loop.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl9013_range_entry_loop.ts):

```ts
// NL9013: a value entering a range inside a loop, with nothing that proves it
// already lies there, keeps its check on every pass and names the guard that
// would prove it.
export const total = (xs: i32[]): i32 => {
  let sum = 0
  for (let k = 0; k < xs.length; k++) {
    const slot: integer<0, 63> = k
    sum = sum + slot
  }
  return sum
}
```

```text
`k` is not proven to lie in integer<0, 63> here, so entering the range keeps its check on every iteration of this loop: guard it with a test that reaches it — `if (k >= 0 && k <= 63)` proves it
```

## NL9016

The message of a warning `--no-warn-performance` turns off contains:

```text
…drops the one the pass before gave it…
```

[`nl9016_arena_pass_drop.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl9016_arena_pass_drop.ts):

```ts
// NL9016: a local declared outside a loop and given a new allocation on every
// pass drops the value the pass before gave it.
export const lastLine = (rows: i32): i32 => {
  let last = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
    last = `row ${i}`;
  }
  return last.length;
};
```

```text
`last` is given a new allocation on every pass of this loop and drops the one the pass before gave it: nothing can reach that value again and nothing frees it while the loop runs, so memory grows with every pass. Declare `last` with `const` inside the loop when only its pass reads it, or keep what the last pass needs as numbers and build the value once after the loop
```

## NL9017

The message of a warning `--no-warn-performance` turns off contains:

```text
… functions, more than eight, so it branches on a `switch` of them where a direct call would not…
```

[`nl9017_fnref_wide_set.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl9017_fnref_wide_set.ts):

```ts
// NL9017: a call through a reference whose set holds more than eight
// functions branches on a `switch` of them where a direct call would not.
function f0(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 0;
}

function f1(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 1;
}

function f2(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 2;
}

function f3(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 3;
}

function f4(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 4;
}

function f5(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 5;
}

function f6(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 6;
}

function f7(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 7;
}

function f8(x: i32): i32 {
  return x + 8;
}

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const ops: ((x: i32) => i32)[] = [f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6, f7, f8];
  let total = 0;
  for (const op of ops) {
    total = total + op(2);
  }
  return total;
};
```

```text
this call through `op` can reach 9 functions, more than eight, so it branches on a `switch` of them where a direct call would not; they came in through `ops: ((x: i32) => i32)[] = [f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6, f7, f8]` (nl9017_fnref_wide_set.ts:40)
```
